content.text:
If you mean **free SiriusXM / satellite radio**:

- **SiriusXM is not permanently free**; it normally requires a paid subscription. SiriusXM says its services require a subscription. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/trial-benefits?utm_source=openai))
- You can usually get a **free trial** through SiriusXM, especially if you have a car with an inactive or newly activated satellite radio. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/free-trial?utm_source=openai))
- SiriusXM also runs occasional **“Listen Free” events** for inactive car radios, but these are limited-time promotions, not year-round free service. A recent 2026 event was listed for **May 21–June 1, 2026**. ([seniordaily.com](https://www.seniordaily.com/siriusxm-free-listen-preview/?utm_source=openai))
- Be careful with “free satellite radio” hacks or codes—unauthorized access is not legal and typically won’t work with modern SiriusXM equipment.

If you just want **free radio-like listening**, use internet radio apps instead:

- **iHeartRadio** — free live local radio and stations  
- **TuneIn** — free ad-supported radio streams  
- **Audacy** — free U.S. radio stations  
- **Radio Garden** — free worldwide radio map  
- **BBC Sounds** — free BBC radio, podcasts, and on-demand audio ([whathifi.com](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-free-music-apps-free-music-on-android-and-iphone?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me your setup — **car radio, home receiver, phone app, or computer** — I can point you to the best free option.
